title: Reserved pool migration: tenant quota reconciliation and rollover safety
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Problem: When tenants are moved between reserved GPU pools (for capacity rebalancing or hardware maintenance) some tenant-level quota state (rolling window usage, burst credits, and monthly anchored offsets) can be double-counted, lost, or mis-anchored to the wrong pool epoch. This leads to incorrect rate limiting, unexpected overages, and customer-reported SLA violations.

This ticket scopes the reconciliation logic and safe rollover path for reserved-pool migrations: ensure tenant usage windows, remaining burst tokens, and future scheduled top-ups are migrated atomically and deterministically with strong invariants against duplication or loss. The goal is to have a migration flow that is reversible within a short window, auditable, and covered by integration + canary rollout tests.
background: We introduced multi-pool reserved capacity in 2025 to improve utilization. Current migration tooling moves compute leases first and then asynchronously copies quota metadata. Edge cases have been observed: (1) tenant has a partially-consumed burst bucket that gets reinitialized when attached to the target pool; (2) the migration replays recent usage events after copy, causing double-counting; (3) timezone and epoch alignment differences between source and target pool cause anchor drift for monthly resets. Support tickets reported customers seeing immediate quota exhaustion after migration and one case of recipient pool showing negative available tokens.
success_criteria: All tenants migrated show identical available quota and burst tokens within 1 second of cutover (measured by reconciliation test harness)
No duplicate usage events are applied (auditable event idempotence proved by integration tests)
Automatic rollback path can be executed to restore previous quota state within 15 minutes and validated by checksums
No increase in rate-limit or billing-related customer incidents in the first 48 hours post-migration during canary rollout
out_of_scope: Global billing system re-architecture, per-token billing price changes, and non-reserved hosted accounts. This ticket focuses on reserved-pool tenant state and the migration path between pools under the same billing tenant.
design_decisions: Adopt an explicit two-phase migration: (1) snapshot & lock tenant quota state in source pool, (2) apply to target pool in a single atomic operation with compare-and-swap anchored by migration_id
Use event idempotency keys derived from (tenant_id, migration_id, source_epoch) to prevent replay duplicates
Do not rely on eventual log-based copy only; require checksum verification step against source snapshot before commit
Implement 'grace hold' window (default 5 minutes) where both pools accept requests but the router prioritizes the target - this allows clients to drain and provides an automatic reconciliation window
Expose a migration audit record with before/after token counts and a tombstone entry on source to prevent late writes
tradeoffs_and_risks: Longer cutover time for large tenants because of snapshot/verification (tradeoff: correctness vs. migration speed)
Requires router changes to support dual-accept grace hold which adds complexity to request routing and observability
Rollback complexity: if external billing has already charged for token consumption, reversing customer-visible state may require coordination with billing team
Edge case risk with cross-region time drift; mitigation: normalize all quota anchors to UTC and use epoch IDs
implementation_notes: Add migration_id to quota metadata schema (string) and ensure default null for existing tenants
Create a snapshot service endpoint: POST /internal/migrations/snapshot -> returns base64-encoded checksum and state blob reference
Enhance quota-apply worker to accept 'migration_id' and perform CAS using metadata.version
Router change: support header X-Quota-Migration: migration_id for grace hold routing policy
Instrumentation: emit migration.audit.{start|snapshot|apply|verify|commit|rollback} with tenant_id and migration_id tags
tasks: Spec: finalize API shapes and migration states (owner: Marco)
Backend: snapshot service + CAS apply worker (owner: Priya Sharma)
Router: implement grace hold routing and header handling (owner: Diego Ruiz)
Integration tests: harness to simulate concurrent requests, replayed events, and checksum mismatches (owner: QA team)
Observability: dashboards for migration success rate, verification checksum mismatches, and latency impacts (owner: SRE)
Run small canary for non-critical tenants, escalate to larger pools on success (owner: MigrationOps)
Billing coordination and playbook for rollback (owner: Finance Ops)
Documentation: runbook, audit format, and API docs (owner: Technical Writer)
Security review and data retention signoff (owner: Security)
Post-mortem template for incidents related to migration
acceptance_criteria: Unit + integration tests cover normal, concurrent, and failure-modes for migration path
Canary migrations performed on two non-production reserved pools without discrepancy
Checksum verification prevents commit on mismatch and triggers automatic rollback
Migration audit entries are searchable in the console and include before/after token counts
Rollback steps documented and tested end-to-end
test_plan: Simulated traffic spike during migration to ensure bucket enforcement remains consistent
Introduce deliberate replayed usage events to verify idempotence
Simulate partial failures (network partition between snapshot and apply) to exercise automatic rollback
Cross-region migration test with synthetic timezone skew to validate anchor normalization
Performance test: measure additional latency introduced by grace hold routing under 95th/99th percentiles
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal account migrations only, 24h monitoring window
Beta: migrate 5 small customers across 2 pools with SRE on-call and rollback triggers
Canary: migrate 10% of low-risk tenants in a single geographic pool
Full rollout: staged by pool size and business tier with automated pre-checks
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: migration.verify.fail if checksum mismatch rate > 0.1% in 1h
Alert: migration.rollback.exec if rollback is executed more than 3 times in 24h
Dashboard: migration success rate, average cutover time, discrepancy delta distribution
SLO: zero customer-facing quota miscounts for canary + beta within 48h
comments: 2026-03-02 - Ayesha Patel: Initial triage — reproduced double-count issue in staging. Root cause suspected: missing CAS at apply time.
2026-03-04 - Marco Li: Drafted two-phase flow; will prototype snapshot+CAS this week. Blocking: router support for grace hold headers.
2026-03-06 - Priya Sharma: Snapshot service prototype returns consistent checksums for tenant state; edge case: partially-applied scheduled top-ups require explicit 'drain' marker
2026-03-08 - Diego Ruiz: Router change landed in feature branch, needs integration test with quota worker

2026-03-09 - QA: Integration test failing intermittently due to race where late usage events arrive between snapshot and tombstone; proposed mitigation: short drain window and accept-at-source policy for late events during grace hold

2026-03-10 - Ayesha Patel: Decided to default grace hold to 5 minutes and add a migration pre-check that rejects migration if tenant has high write-rate > 200 req/s. Filed follow-up ENG-88124 for autoscheduler integration.
